headline: BTC $84.0k flat into Bitget's 04:00 UTC withdrawal decision; SOL +6.9% week
summary: As of 01:55 UTC on 26 September BTC is $84,052.40 against an $84,090.50 open (-0.05%), sitting 43% up its $83,163.60-$85,247.40 daily band, ETH is $2,693.09 (+0.06%) and the laggard at 34% of a $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range, and SOL is $121.96 (-0.13%) but 87% up its $115.85-$122.91 range after bouncing 5.3% off the $115.85 low, leaving weekly changes at +2.8% BTC, +2.3% ETH and +6.9% SOL. There is no dip on the board right now: all three are flat on the session, Hyperliquid funding is mild at 0.00073%/h for BTC and 0.00125%/h for ETH and SOL, BTC open interest is $3.20bn with the futures premium at -0.045%, so futures are still trading under spot and nobody is paying up to be long. The tape is being set by bonds rather than crypto - the US 10-year is around 5.16-5.21% near 19-year highs after a 58.4 flash PMI, and October Fed hike odds sit near 66-75% - offset by the first real de-escalation headline in months, with US and Iranian negotiators exploring a phased Strait of Hormuz reopening that knocked WTI over $2 lower to $91.74 and let BTC reclaim $84,000. The one open crypto wound is Bitget: $387.5m taken, withdrawals still suspended, and a resumption plan promised by 04:00 UTC today, roughly two hours from this snapshot and into a weekend. Fear & Greed is 74 and the composite reads 61.8, both Greed, on 151 items in 24 hours - a de-levered, range-bound market with one custody question due to resolve overnight.

BTC.note: $84,052.40, unchanged on the session and 43% up an $83,163.60-$85,247.40 band, with open interest at $3.20bn, funding at 0.00073%/h and the futures premium at -0.045% - this is range consolidation after Friday's $15.6bn options expiry cleared, not a dip.

ETH.note: $2,693.09, up 0.06% but the weakest of the three at 34% of a $2,667.23-$2,742.42 range and only +2.3% on the week, on $2.98bn of open interest and a -0.006% premium, so there is neither a crowded long nor an obvious bid here.

SOL.note: $121.96, 87% up its $115.85-$122.91 range after recovering 5.3% off the low, +6.9% on the week and the clear leader, on the thinnest book of the three at $753m of open interest with the Alpenglow mainnet activation two days out.

drivers.title: Bitget still frozen at $387.5m with a plan due 04:00 UTC today
drivers.detail: CEO Gracy Chen put the loss at $387.5m, revised up from $351.6m after Zcash and TRON transfers were traced, and committed to publishing a withdrawal resumption plan by 1 p.m. KST / 04:00 UTC on 26 September; deposits and trading run, withdrawals do not. Circle and Tether froze stablecoins in attacker wallets but most of the funds had already moved, and North Korea is a named suspect.

drivers.title: 10-year near 19-year highs, October hike priced around 70%
drivers.detail: The US 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.16-5.21% after touching its highest level since 2007 this week, and the 58.4 September flash PMI - the fastest expansion since 2021 - pushed CME-implied odds of a 25bp October Fed hike into the 66-75% band. Bond volatility is surging while bitcoin and equities stay comparatively calm, which is what has pinned BTC at the low end of its range all week.

drivers.title: US-Iran explore phased Hormuz reopening; WTI drops to $91.74
drivers.detail: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi handed the US a seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks, with Qatari mediation on the UN General Assembly sidelines and both sides exploring a phased swap of passage for blockade relief. WTI fell more than $2 to $91.74 on the reports and BTC reclaimed $84,000 in the same window - the single cleanest path to lower oil, lower yields and a friendlier tape.

drivers.title: $15.6bn BTC options expired Friday, removing the gamma pin
drivers.detail: About 182,000 BTC of Deribit options - 106,200 calls against 75,900 puts, a 0.71 put/call ratio - expired on 25 September with max pain far below spot near $75,000-$76,000. Dealer hedging around that strike stack had helped hold BTC in its tight band; with more than a third of open contracts settled, that mechanical support is gone and the range can widen in either direction.

drivers.title: Spot BTC ETFs still taking money: ~$191m on 24 September
drivers.detail: US spot bitcoin ETFs drew roughly $191m of net inflows on 24 September, with IBIT at +$162.6m and FBTC at +$12.9m, extending a six-session streak worth about $2.8bn even as BTC sat at the low end of its range. IBIT options pricing has also calmed since the rebound, so the institutional bid has not flinched at the Bitget headlines.

drivers.title: SEC loses its crypto advocate on 2 October, down to two commissioners
drivers.detail: Hester Peirce, who led the SEC's Crypto Task Force, posted a resignation letter on 25 September setting her last day at 2 October, leaving the agency with only Chair Atkins and Mark Uyeda - a bare quorum - to carry the token classification and registration rulemaking. It lands two weeks after the Senate's CLARITY Act cloture vote failed and as the Blockchain Association changes leadership, so the US regulatory calendar has slipped further out.

watch.what: Bitget's committed deadline (1 p.m. KST) to publish its withdrawal resumption plan. Note the wording: the promise is a plan, not necessarily an immediate reopening. A clean, dated reopening closes the only acute crypto story on the board; a second slip - the timetable already moved once while the loss estimate rose 10% - into a thin weekend book is the item most able to turn a contained exchange loss into a broader question about exchange balances.

Solana's Alpenglow mainnet activation via the Agave 4.3 feature gate: Votor replaces TowerBFT, finality targets ~150ms versus ~12.8s, and fault tolerance rises from 33% to 40%. Validators that failed to register a BLS key on-chain are excluded from the consensus set. It lands on the thinnest book of the three ($753m open interest) after a +6.9% week, so SOL carries the most positioning risk into it.

JOLTS job openings, Chicago PMI, FHFA House Price Index and CB Consumer Confidence, all on quarter-end when flows get pushed around. With October hike odds already near 70%, a hot labour-demand print firms the hike and is the most direct scheduled pressure on dip-buying next week.
ADP Employment Change and ISM Manufacturing PMI. The read-through to Friday's payrolls, against a flash composite PMI that already printed 58.4.

September Employment Situation - nonfarm payrolls and unemployment (08:30 ET). Same day, Hester Peirce's last day at the SEC. First-Friday payrolls into a Fed markets already expect to hike on 28 October.

US-Iran technical talks on the phased Hormuz reopening, against Tehran's seven-day proposal tied to lifting the naval blockade. Progress is the cleanest route to lower oil and lower yields; a collapse puts the 10-year back at 19-year highs and BTC back toward $83,163.
FOMC rate decision (2:00 p.m. ET). The meeting everything above is pricing into; the current market-implied probability of a 25bp hike is roughly 66-75%.
